title: Ops Corridor: taskified runbook orchestration and safe admin utilities
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Our current runbooks are prose-heavy, hard to compose, and often executed ad-hoc by oncall engineers. This leads to variance in remediation steps, longer MTTR, and limited reuse across teams.

Goal: Build the 'Ops Corridor' — a lightweight orchestration and execution layer that converts canonical runbooks into composable, auditable tasklets that can be invoked by admin utilities (CLI, Console quick-actions, and programmatic APIs). The corridor must provide simulation/dry-run, RBAC gating, per-step approval, and immutable audit traces.

Scope and non-goals: Scope includes: runbook->tasklet compiler, a small execution runtime that enforces safety policies, Console UI for approving/launching tasklets, CLI adapters, and telemetry hooks for cost/latency and success rates. Non-goal: this iteration will NOT replace full incident automation engines; we are focusing on human-in-the-loop and safe one-click remediations.

Success metrics: 20% reduction in median MTTR for P2 incidents driven by runbookable remediation; 40% reuse rate of tasklets across two or more teams within 2 months; zero-security-finding in review; audit log retention for 90 days.

Design notes and trade-offs:
- Representation: We use a JSONL tasklet format (steps with typed inputs/outputs) to stay language-agnostic and easy to version. Trade-off: smaller upfront parsing vs. future DSL expressivity.
- Safety model: Opt-in per-step approval + policy engine that can require escalation for high-impact actions (RBAC + approver groups). Trade-off: slightly higher click friction vs. reduced blast radius.
- Execution runtime: lightweight, single-process coordinator that calls existing admin utilities (ops-cli and internal REST admin endpoints). Avoid spinning up full workers in this phase to reduce infra changes.
- Observability: emit structured traces for each step with tokenized cost estimates, plus a binary success/failure signal. Integrate with Console traces and existing telemetry pipeline.

Implementation plan (phases):
1) Converter circuit (2w): author a tool that converts canonical runbooks (Confluence/Markdown) into canonical tasklet JSONL. Includes a small schema and validation.
2) Runtime & safety layer (3w): runtime that executes steplets, enforces policy, supports dry-run, and records audit events.
3) Console + CLI integration (2w): Console quick-action card and ops-cli adapter to discover, preview, and execute tasklets.
4) Pilot & measurements (2w): onboard Trust & Infra teams for pilot, collect MTTR and telemetry, iterate on policies.

Open items:
- Policy language: use existing RBAC/approval groups or add policy DSL? (PM prefers reuse; security requests a small policy DSL).
- Schema fields for long-running steps and cancellation behavior.
- How to surface simulated side-effects in Console without leaking secrets.

Links:

Safety checklist: require SSO-enforced approver groups, KMS-backed audit log encryption, and automated smoke-run tests in CI.
